query: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy with excellent mechanical properties at 1600 °C but very poor room-temperature ductility, while its irradiation resistance has primarily been proposed by first-principles calculations. What intervention could improve its room-temperature ductility without compromising its high-temperature mechanical performance or irradiation resistance? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline under room-temperature, 1600 °C, and irradiation assessments, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a controlled amount of Re to equiatomic NbMoTaW will improve its room-temperature ductility by refining the grain structure and introducing amorphous intergranular films without compromising its high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, single-phase, BCC NbMoTaW films (magnetron-sputtered, columnar nanocrystalline microstructure) that exhibit excellent high-temperature mechanical performance but poor room-temperature ductility.
generation.intervention: Incorporate an appropriate fraction of Re (e.g., modifying composition to Nb20Mo20Ta20W20Re20 at.%) during film deposition to form a Re-doped variant.
generation.conditions: Films are prepared by magnetron sputtering at room temperature under similar deposition parameters. Evaluations include room-temperature ductility tests (nanoindentation and micropillar compression), high-temperature mechanical tests at 1600 °C, and irradiation studies using 120 keV He2+ at a fluence of 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2.
generation.structural_mediator: Re addition refines the grain size, enhances lattice distortion, increases excess free volume, and forms several-nanometer-wide amorphous regions at grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure and amorphous intergranular films serve as defect sinks that not only enable more uniform plastic deformation (improving room-temperature ductility) but also stabilize the BCC phase and mitigate the accumulation of irradiation-induced He bubbles. This balance preserves high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated NbMoTaW baseline, the Re-containing alloy will exhibit significantly enhanced ductility at room temperature while maintaining similar high-temperature mechanical performance at 1600 °C and showing reduced He-bubble segregation and irradiation-induced hardening.
generation.baseline: The performance of untreated equiatomic NbMoTaW films, which already demonstrate excellent mechanical performance at 1600 °C but poor ductility and marked grain-boundary He bubble formation under irradiation.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to magnetron-sputtered films with similar nanocrystalline morphology and under the specified irradiation conditions (120 keV He2+ at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2). Effects may vary with different processing methods, microstructures, or irradiation environments.
generation.uncertainty: The exact optimal concentration of Re and the extent of grain refinement or amorphous boundary formation needed to achieve the desired balance remain to be fully determined.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two series of films under identical conditions: one series of pure NbMoTaW and one series of NbMoTaW with the Re adjustment. Characterize microstructural features by TEM (grain size, amorphous boundary width) and XRD (phase stability). Perform room-temperature nanoindentation and micropillar compression tests for ductility assessment, conduct high-temperature (1600 °C) mechanical tests, and expose both series to 120 keV He2+ irradiation at 1 × 10^16 ions/cm^2. Compare the ductility, high-temperature strength, and irradiation damage signatures (He bubble size/distribution) of the two series.
measurements: TEM measurements of grain size and detection of amorphous regions at grain boundaries
Nanoindentation and micropillar compression load–displacement curves
Post-irradiation assessment of He bubble size/distribution and irradiation-induced hardening via TEM and nanoindentation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Re-doped NbMoTaW films do not show a statistically significant improvement in room-temperature ductility, or if high-temperature performance or irradiation resistance is degraded relative to the pure NbMoTaW baseline, the hypothesis will be rejected.
